_comment: The project register. Every project appears, started or not. Grouped by Branch, the taxonomy from the FutureMap READMEs. Status is honest: 'working' means it runs, 'partial' means some of it runs, 'scaffold' means a README and a stub, 'planned' means a description and no code. Owner ruling 2026-08-31: presenting unstarted work as unstarted is the point, not a weakness.

projects.name: Dungeon Cue
projects.one_line: Say the phrase, the rain starts, nobody at the table looks up.
projects.detail: Windows desktop app. Modes, sound sets, four configurable buttons, wake and sleep phrases, and an auto-switch on 'Roll for Initiative' because that sentence is already said out loud at exactly the right moment. It produces no audio itself; every trigger is a call relayed by Syrinscape's servers to a player logged into your account. Android exists as a push-to-talk skeleton.
projects.state_note: Finished and on sale. Review copies out with creators.

projects.name: CampaignOS
projects.one_line: Voice-first live session runner for D&D 5e. A second screen that keeps combat moving while you talk.
projects.detail: Tauri v2, Rust backend, vanilla webview HUD, roughly 15 MB binary. Event-sourced state with undo and redo. The Drum (combat and initiative HUD) is operational. Tier-1 natural language parser handles table speech like '5 on goblin 1' in under 2ms at zero token cost. Player View runs on a second screen with sanitised combatant cards.
projects.state_note: Modules 1 through 7 built or partial. The Vault and The Arbiter scoped to v1.5, The Forge and The Loom to v2.0, deliberately, to protect a fifteen-minute onboarding.

projects.name: DM Toolbox
projects.one_line: Zero-dependency desktop suite of ten GM tools in one standalone executable.
projects.detail: Ten modules planned: Dungeon Cue audio bridge as the flagship, plus Combat Engine, Session Prep Wizard, Faction Web, Handout Props, Recap Cards, AI Sidekick Sim, Codex, Rules Lawyer, Loot Ledger. Shares the SoundCue visual language.
projects.state_note: Draft plan, generated briefs, research. No application yet.

projects.name: SoundCue
projects.one_line: A soundboard that listens to the room and fires the sound when it hears the phrase.
projects.detail: Dungeon Cue proved the idea on a chunked Python pipeline that was slow and clunky, and this is the proper version of it: Flutter, on-device phrase spotting, Windows and phone from one codebase. Audio is processed in memory and never written to disk or uploaded, which is an architectural rule rather than a setting. Local playback is only one output. The same trigger can press a button in Companion, send OSC to a lighting desk, or fire a MIDI note, so it drives the tools someone already owns instead of competing with them.
projects.state_note: Needs testing. That is the only thing standing between it and finished. The name is a working codename and collides with existing apps, so it changes before anything public.

projects.name: MudBuddy
projects.one_line: Watches you play a text MUD and suggests the next command. It never types anything itself.
projects.detail: You stay the only thing touching the game, which is the design, not a limitation. It proposes a command with a stated guess about what will happen and a window in which the guess still counts, then watches whether you did it and whether the prediction held. Ignoring a suggestion three times in the same situation lowers its weight, because you knowing better is also information.

projects.name: AxiomTEA
projects.one_line: Reads an engineering pitch and tells you which numbers are physically impossible. No language model anywhere near the verdict.
projects.detail: Deterministic first-principles diligence engine. Extracts quantitative claims, checks them against physical law and cited literature, and renders one analysis across ten stakeholder lenses that cannot contradict each other. Runs entirely offline; exactly one module is permitted outbound HTTPS and it handles data updates only. Ships as a single self-contained executable.
projects.state_note: Version 5.0.0. 41 of 41 tests passing as of 2026-08-21, the only verified project in the FutureMap set. Health endpoint reports the exact bundled dependency versions, because a binary once shipped silently missing one.

projects.name: SynapseGraph
projects.one_line: Turns a pile of scientific PDFs into a graph you can actually ask questions of.
projects.detail: Research sits locked in documents built to be printed, not searched, so finding what connects to what means reading all of it and remembering all of it. This pulls the structure out and builds the cross-references itself.

branches.branch: Branch 24 and 2: Multi-agent systems and orchestration

projects.name: AmoebiX
projects.one_line: The arm rack. A local toolbox that dispatches questions to many models, keeps the answers, and logs what came of them.
projects.detail: Panel runs against a library of lenses, multi-model quorum, sensory collection, task cards, decision logging, and an append-only event ledger. Thirty-two configured models across API, browser and CLI backends. Results are SHA-256 cached so an identical rerun costs nothing. The editor lens lives here and works.
projects.state_note: In daily use. Nine lenses rewritten for this brand on 2026-08-31. Synod was a part of this, not a separate thing, and no longer exists under its own name.

projects.name: AGY Bridge
projects.one_line: Drops a task in a folder so a coding agent inside an IDE picks it up, does the work, and reports back.
projects.detail: The IDE has no doorbell. Nothing outside it can ring, and only its command line can be triggered from elsewhere, so the bridge is a watched folder. A brief goes into the inbox, a watcher spins the agent up against it, and a result lands in the outbox carrying a status: pending, in progress, done, blocked, or failed. One rule holds the rest together. Only the completion command may write DONE, so an agent that crashes has to leave its brief visibly unfinished. That rule exists because this bridge reported a false DONE once already.
projects.state_note: Working, with two lessons built into it. One target per brief and a ten minute budget, after a five target brief ran out of time having already found its answers and threw the work away. And briefs are shaped as goals rather than methods: say what done looks like and what the bar is, and it reads the code and works out how. Asked to attack a system as an adversary rather than review it, it found four silent faults the author's own attacks had missed.

projects.name: AegisBox
projects.one_line: Runs an agent's code in a box where it can only touch what you handed it.
projects.detail: An agent that writes and executes its own code is one bad line from deleting your files or posting them somewhere. This gives it a floor, four walls, and no exit you did not open yourself.

projects.name: AgentMesh
projects.one_line: Lets agents find and borrow each other's tools without anyone wiring them together first.
projects.detail: Agents end up siloed because connecting any two of them means hand-writing an integration for that exact pair, and the number of pairs grows faster than anyone can keep up with. This is the protocol for one to discover what another can do and negotiate the use of it.

branches.branch: Branch 1 and 23: Cognitive architectures and interpretability

projects.name: AxiomVerify
projects.one_line: Checks whether an argument follows, step by step, instead of whether it sounds like it does.
projects.detail: Models make invalid logical jumps and write them fluently, which is the worst possible combination in maths, law and code. This walks the structure of the argument and names the step where the deduction breaks.

projects.name: NeuroSteer
projects.one_line: Turns one idea up or down inside a running model, and shows you all three results side by side.
projects.detail: Steering a model normally means retraining it or arguing with it in the prompt. This reaches into the layers while it generates, amplifies or suppresses a single concept, and prints the untouched version next to the amplified and the suppressed so you can see what the change actually did rather than what it was supposed to do.

projects.name: GridPulse VPP
projects.one_line: Moves heavy compute to the hours when the grid has power going spare.
projects.detail: Training clusters and industrial pumps pull hardest whenever is convenient, which is how congestion and a large bill arrive together. This schedules the load against what the grid and the weather are doing.

projects.name: FlowGrid
projects.one_line: Works out whether a flow battery pays for itself across a windless week.
projects.detail: Lithium storage stops making economic sense past about eight hours because its power cost and its energy cost are welded together. Flow batteries pull those apart, and this runs the numbers on whether that is worth it for a given site and a given stretch of cloud.

projects.name: EpiGuide
projects.one_line: Designs CRISPR guides that switch a gene off without cutting the DNA.
projects.detail: Cutting both strands risks chromosome damage the cell cannot always repair cleanly. Methylation quiets the gene and leaves the sequence intact, which is what you want when the goal is to turn something down rather than remove it.

projects.name: CrystalGen
projects.one_line: Predicts whether a proposed crystal would survive being made.
projects.detail: Finding a new superconductor or a solid battery electrolyte has historically meant years of mixing things and seeing what holds together. This screens the candidate for stability before anyone books lab time.

projects.name: AquaNutrient
projects.one_line: Holds a hydroponic system's water chemistry steady without anyone watching it.
projects.detail: Farming loses most of its fresh water to runoff and evaporation. Hydroponics trades that for pH swings and nutrient lock-out, which can ruin a crop quietly between two visits. This keeps the balance and logs every correction it made.

branches.branch: Branch 3, 9 and 12: Robotics, transit, neural interfaces

projects.name: Kinematix
projects.one_line: Keeps a two-legged robot standing when something shoves it.
projects.detail: Bipedal robots fall on uneven ground and in the fall the expensive parts break. This is the balance controller that has to react to a sideways push in the moment before the fall commits.

projects.name: OmniFleet
projects.one_line: Sends robotaxis where the passengers will be, before they are there.
projects.detail: An empty car driving to a pickup earns nothing and spends battery doing it, and the surge always arrives faster than a fleet repositions. This is the dispatch and charging schedule that moves early instead of catching up.

projects.name: SynapseDecode
projects.one_line: Turns raw neural spikes into smooth limb movement in under twenty milliseconds.
projects.detail: A prosthetic that lags feels like it belongs to somebody else. The decoder has to translate chaotic firing across many channels into continuous motion fast enough that the intention and the movement land as one event.

projects.name: SovereignVault
projects.one_line: Your data in a store you hold the keys to, rather than one you rent.
projects.detail: A central cloud database is one place to breach, one company to be locked into, and one log nobody outside can read. This keeps the data with the person it belongs to.

projects.name: Draega
projects.one_line: A world of twelve continents, two moons that are never not full, and a history reaching back a hundred and twenty three million years.
projects.detail: Published on World Anvil, owner-authored throughout. Thirty-two articles covering continents, oceans, settlements and a dated history timeline.

projects.name: Golden Sea campaign kit
projects.one_line: Twenty-four modules, a session master doc, and per-module stat kits for a campaign across the Draega archipelago.
projects.state_note: Ready for further work, not ready for dispersion. Presentation is the gap, not structure.

projects.name: Rivals and Destiny podcast
projects.one_line: Twenty-five sessions, an archipelago, and a war between an empire that wanted everything and a rebellion that could not afford to lose.
projects.state_note: Recorded, not released. Its own lifecycle, beside the rest of this rather than inside it.

projects.name: mAxAdrAgoN
projects.one_line: This site. A running record of the work, with a register of every project and a page for the finished ones.
projects.detail: Plain HTML and vanilla JavaScript reading JSON files. No framework and no build step, which means a change to what the site says is an edit to data rather than a deployment. A validator runs six checks and refuses the push if any fail, and it has already caught real faults: an encoding mark that broke a file's frontmatter, and a legal notice missing from three pages.

projects.name: Windows runner
projects.one_line: A folder that runs PowerShell on this machine, so an assistant in a data centre can act on it without a port open.
projects.detail: An assistant in the cloud cannot reach this computer. The usual answer is a chat window full of commands and a person pasting them one at a time, which is the problem wearing a solution costume. Instead a small loop watches a queue directory, runs any script that appears there, and moves it aside when it finishes. Nothing listens for a connection, so nothing can connect. The only way in is writing a file into one folder, and only something already trusted with the disk can do that.
